'''Alternate Image''' ('''AI''') is a Decipher printing of a rare with different artwork and the same title, lore, statistics, and game text. That printing is titled ''Title (AI)''.

Decipher packed twenty-seven Alternate Image rares in three Episode I expansions: [[Tatooine]] (May 2001), [[Coruscant]] (August 2001), and [[Theed Palace]] (December 2001), nine in each set.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 14, 16, 18, 49. [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ Collecting] at starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20141218160433/http://www.starwarsccg.org:80/collecting/ Internet Archive].</ref> Earlier Decipher expansions did not pack AI rares. The [[Players Committee]] later issued virtual Alternate Image cards; those are a separate product.<ref name="official-ai">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/virtual/Official_Alternate_Images_2024.pdf Official Alternate Images], SWCCG Players Committee (updated December 2023). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165223/https://res.starwarsccg.org/virtual/Official_Alternate_Images_2024.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Identification ==

Printed Alternate Image cards are marked by a gold ring around the expansion icon. The matching regular printing has a gray or silver ring.<ref name="arb">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2022/SWCCG_2022_AdvancedRulebook.pdf SWCCG Advanced Rulebook] (2022), Alternate Image Cards. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165106/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2022/SWCCG_2022_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]].</ref><ref name="tat-rules">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/tatooinerules.pdf Tatooine Expansion Set Rule Page], Decipher (2001). The Light and Dark checklists print a second line ''Alternate image (Gold icon)'' under each matching rare. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009171513/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/tatooinerules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="swu">[https://www.starwars-universe.com/collectionnables-serie-53-tatooine-ccg.html Tatooine (CCG)], Star Wars Universe. The French checklist identifies Alternate Image cards by the ''halo doré'' around the set logo.</ref> Collectors on BoardGameGeek in 2005 wrote that the metallic ring is silver or bronze/gold and that a magnifying glass is sometimes needed to tell the printings apart.<ref name="bgg-2005">[https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/86028/two-more-collectors-questions Two more collector's questions], BoardGameGeek (8 November 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009170119/https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/86028/two-more-collectors-questions Internet Archive].</ref> The gold ring does not change the expansion icon for rules purposes.<ref name="arb" />

The SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia and CardGuide list the subset as rarity '''#A''' (Alternate Image Card).<ref name="encyc" /><ref name="cardguide">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Star Wars CCG Complete Card List 4.0], Key To Rarity: ''#A — Alternate Image Card''. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20210630004212/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Packing and rarity ==

Each of the three Episode I expansions sold 11-card packs (MSRP $3.29) whose last card was a rare or an Alternate Image. Encyclopedia 3.2 labels that slot ''Mains / Alternate Image''.<ref name="encyc" /> The AI versions sit on the rare sheet as a subset of the matching title, so they are scarcer than the regular printing of the same card. On [[Tatooine]], two of eight sheet copies of those titles are the Alternate Image (one in four copies of that title).<ref name="encyc" />

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Set !! AI rares !! Sheet ratio (AI of that title) !! Exceptions
|-
| [[Tatooine]] (May 2001) || 9 (5 Light, 4 Dark) || 2 of 8 copies || [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] nine times per side
|-
| [[Coruscant]] (August 2001) || 9 (6 Light, 3 Dark) || 1 of 4 copies || [[Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber]] Light and [[Dioxis]] Dark five times each
|-
| [[Theed Palace]] (December 2001) || 9 (6 Light, 3 Dark) || 2 of 6 copies || [[Naboo Celebration]] Light and [[Master, Destroyers!]] Dark seven times each
|}

Those sheet counts are from Encyclopedia 3.2.<ref name="encyc" /> Because only nine titles in each set have an AI version, a random pack is more likely to contain a regular rare. From the 11&times;11 rare sheets, about one in thirteen [[Tatooine]] or [[Theed Palace]] packs contains an Alternate Image, and about one in twenty-seven [[Coruscant]] packs contains one (Coruscant has sixty rares on the sheet rather than thirty or forty).<ref name="encyc" />

== Gameplay ==

Card identity is the title. An Alternate Image and the matching regular printing are the same card: both are lost from hand to [[Monnok]], and uniqueness is shared.<ref name="glossary">[[Media:Decipher_Glossary_Supplement.pdf|Decipher Glossary Supplement]] (updated 29 January 2002), entry ''alternate image cards''.</ref><ref name="arb" />

The gold ring does not change the expansion icon, so an Alternate Image does not allow a persona replace that the regular printing would not allow. A player may not persona replace [[Queen Amidala, Ruler Of Naboo]] with [[Queen Amidala]] even when one of those cards is an Alternate Image.<ref name="arb" />

== Collecting ==

Collectors pay more for the Alternate Image than for the matching regular printing of the same title. CategoryOneGames retail listings on 9 October 2026 show that gap on several titles:

* [[Mace Windu (AI)]] ([[Coruscant]]) out of stock at $79.99; the regular [[Mace Windu]] from the same set listed Mint/Near Mint at $29.99.<ref name="c1-mace-ai">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/mace_windu_alternative_image/54777 Mace Windu (Alternative Image)], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165245/https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/mace_windu_alternative_image/54777 Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="c1-mace-reg">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/mace_windu/54775 Mace Windu], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). The Alternate Image catalog page lists this regular printing Mint/Near Mint at $29.99.</ref>
* [[Darth Maul, Young Apprentice (AI)]] ([[Coruscant]]) Lightly Played at $287.99; the regular [[Darth Maul, Young Apprentice]] Lightly Played at $44.99.<ref name="c1-maulya-ai">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/darth_maul_young_apprentice_alternative_image/54737 Darth Maul, Young Apprentice (Alternative Image)], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165410/https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/darth_maul_young_apprentice_alternative_image/54737 Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="c1-maulya-reg">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/darth_maul_young_apprentice/54736 Darth Maul, Young Apprentice], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165512/https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_coruscant/darth_maul_young_apprentice/54736 Internet Archive].</ref>
* [[Mace Windu, Jedi Master (AI)]] ([[Theed Palace]]) Lightly Played at $67.49, Moderately Played at $59.99, Heavily Played at $52.49.<ref name="c1-mace-theed">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_theed_palace/mace_windu_jedi_master_alternative_image/54628 Mace Windu, Jedi Master (Alternative Image)], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165621/https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-swccg_theed_palace/mace_windu_jedi_master_alternative_image/54628 Internet Archive].</ref>

Those figures are dated dealer snapshots, not a standing price guide. Premiums vary by title, condition, and whether [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]] later foiled that Alternate Image. The Star Wars Collectors Archive records foil reprints of [[Qui-Gon Jinn (AI)]] and [[Darth Maul (AI)]] in Reflections III.<ref name="swca-quigon">[http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=68441 Reflections III, Light Side, Foil, Qui-Gon Jinn (Alternate Image)], Star Wars Collectors Archive. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20130621050736/http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=68441 Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="swca-maul">[http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=68363 Reflections III, Dark Side, Foil, Darth Maul (Alternate Image)], Star Wars Collectors Archive. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20130621064725/http://theswca.com/index.php?action=disp_item&item_id=68363 Internet Archive].</ref> CategoryOneGames listed the Qui-Gon Jinn Alternate Image foil Lightly Played at $242.99 on 9 October 2026.<ref name="c1-quigon-foil">[https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-reflections_iii_foil/quigon_jinn_alternative_image_foil/58768 Qui-Gon Jinn (Alternative Image) (Foil)], CategoryOneGames (catalog, retrieved 9 October 2026). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009165756/https://www.categoryonegames.com/catalog/star_wars_ccg-reflections_iii_foil/quigon_jinn_alternative_image_foil/58768 Internet Archive].</ref>

Decipher's complete American card list dated 23 August 2001 records a last update for "minor corrections and addition of alternate image cards," after [[Tatooine]] and during the [[Coruscant]] window.<ref name="swallcards">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Complete Card List], Decipher (updated 23 August 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

A published Decipher designer interview that explains why the company packed Alternate Image rares has not been located. The packing, gold-ring mark, and gameplay identity are documented in Decipher's Glossary Supplement, the Tatooine rules/checklist card, the Players Committee Advanced Rulebook, and Encyclopedia 3.2.

== Virtual Alternate Images ==

The Players Committee issues virtual Alternate Image cards as a later product, separate from the twenty-seven Decipher-printed rares. The committee's ''Official Alternate Images'' list (updated December 2023) states that those virtual cards are tournament legal. Year headings on that list mark when an AI became publicly available; most virtual AIs are exclusive prizes for two years before that public release.<ref name="official-ai" />
